PullRequest.Title: chat: fix click focus outline and chevron size on collapsible notices
PullRequest.Body:

Collapsible system notices in chat, such as the artifact Autopilot updates ("Autopilot updated for … (5 rules)"), had two visual problems:

- Clicking the notice left the workbench focus outline around it. The outline should only appear for keyboard navigation.
- The disclosure chevron rendered at the base codicon size instead of the compact size that thinking and tool group headers use.

### Changes

- The header's focus outline is suppressed for pointer focus only (`:focus:not(:focus-visible)`), so keyboard focus still shows it.
- The chevron's compact size is now declared with enough specificity to outrank `.monaco-workbench .codicon[class*='codicon-']`, which was resetting it to the base size. The chevron was already compact outside a workbench ancestor, which is why the existing tests did not catch this.
- A regression test renders the notice under a `.monaco-workbench` ancestor with the workbench stylesheet loaded and checks the chevron's computed size.

### How to test

1. Show a collapsible system notice in chat, for example by changing the Autopilot rules of a pull request artifact in an Agent Host session, or open the `chat/chatArtifactAutomation` component fixtures.
2. Click the notice. It expands and collapses without a focus outline.
3. Tab to the notice. The focus outline appears, and Enter toggles the details.
4. Compare the chevron with a thinking or tool group header. They are the same size.

### Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatContentParts/chatSystemNotificationContentPart.test.ts`: 15 passing. The new test fails without the stylesheet change, where the chevron computes to `16px` instead of `12px`.
- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- `pnpm run stylelint`: passed, with no findings for the changed stylesheet.
- `pnpm run oxlint src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/chatContentParts/chatSystemNotificationContentPart.test.ts`: passed.
- The `chat/chatArtifactAutomation` component fixtures render without errors. There, a real mouse click leaves no outline, keyboard focus shows it, and the chevron computes to `12px`.

### Before / After

Recorded in the `chat/chatArtifactAutomation/AllPullRequestAutopilotsExpanded` component fixture with real mouse and keyboard input. The "before" half uses the stylesheet from `main`.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render a chat response containing collapsible system notifications
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The chat list renderer creates one ChatSystemNotificationContentPart per notification, renders its summary/details DOM, then browser style calculation matches the two added selectors. The diff adds no script, layout read, or asynchronous prerequisite to rendering.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales with rendered collapsible notification elements. The new font-size selector matches only the single disclosure chevron under each notification, while the focus selector can match only its header.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Rendering remains synchronous per visible chat row under the existing chat list renderer; the diff adds no tasks, queueing, IPC, or parallel work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No application cache, network cache, or negative-cache behavior is involved. Normal browser stylesheet/CSSOM reuse is unchanged; the production stylesheet was already loaded by the component.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: the changed production lines are declarative focus/size rules only, and the traced constructor and renderer path show no newly reached expensive boundary.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact CSS selector-match cost varies by browser and transcript size, but both selectors are narrowly scoped and add constant work per rendered notification, with no forced layout or retained state.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added CSS performs bounded selector matching on existing DOM nodes and does not add synchronous geometry reads, rendering loops, allocations, or boundary calls.

Scenarios.Scenario: Pointer click or keyboard focus toggles a collapsible system-notification disclosure
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing Button focus/click handling updates pseudo-class state and toggles existing classes/ARIA attributes. The new :focus:not(:focus-visible) rule only changes outline painting, and the chevron font-size is already resolved from the loaded stylesheet; no added work blocks interaction.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Each interaction affects one notification header and chevron regardless of transcript length; selector invalidation is limited by the scoped class chain.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One synchronous interaction handler runs for the targeted disclosure. The diff introduces no concurrency, retries, or fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache behavior is changed. Stylesheet and font assets follow the existing workbench loading path; no new fetch is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the added selectors and existing click handler: only style resolution/painting changes on an already interactive element.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser style invalidation details vary, but the affected subtree is a single disclosure and the change does not read geometry or rebuild DOM.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Interaction remains bounded to one existing component, with no added layout-forcing operation, expensive boundary, or retained resource.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the full two-file diff. Production changes are two narrowly scoped CSS declarations; the only stylesheet import added is test-only. Traced chat rendering and interaction paths, selector cardinality, lifecycle, and all transitive expensive boundaries; no actionable diff-introduced performance regression or qualifying regression fix was found.
